topics.title: The cell
topics.concept: Cell theory, microscope, cell structure (plant, animal, prokaryotic) and transport across membranes.

subtopics.title: Cell theory and the microscope
subtopics.concept: Cell theory: all living things are made of cells; the cell is the smallest unit of life; cells come from pre-existing cells. Microscope: the revolving nose piece rotates the objective lenses into position.

subtopics.title: Cell structure
subtopics.concept: All cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and genetic material (nucleus in eukaryotes). Organelles lie in the cytoplasm. Plant cells have cell walls and chloroplasts; bacteria have cell walls but no membrane-bound organelles.

subtopics.title: Transport across the cell membrane
subtopics.concept: Diffusion, osmosis and facilitated diffusion move substances down a concentration gradient; active transport uses energy (ATP) to move them against it.

subtopics.title: Characteristics of living things
subtopics.concept: Living things are made of cells, grow and develop, reproduce, respond to stimuli, respire/use energy (metabolism), excrete, move, and maintain homeostasis.

topics.title: Diversity of living things
topics.concept: Kingdoms Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia; their structure, nutrition, reproduction and economic importance.

subtopics.title: Kingdom Monera (bacteria, cyanobacteria)
subtopics.concept: Unicellular prokaryotes; shapes rods (bacilli), spheres (cocci) and spirals (spirilla); cell walls of peptidoglycan (not chitin); autotrophic (photosynthetic/chemosynthetic) or heterotrophic (saprophytes, parasites). Cyanobacteria with red pigment periodically colour the Red Sea; they reproduce by cell division or fragmentation.

subtopics.title: Kingdom Protista (protozoa and algae)
subtopics.concept: Euglena, Entamoeba, Paramecium, Plasmodium, Chlamydomonas and Spirogyra are protists. Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga with spiral chloroplasts; it reproduces by simple cell division (fission) and, in unfavourable conditions, by conjugation.

subtopics.title: Kingdom Fungi
subtopics.concept: Fungi have chitin cell walls. Yeasts ferment sugar for bread, beer and wine and reproduce by budding; Penicillium gives the antibiotic penicillin; some fungi are pathogens.

topics.title: Nutrition and metabolism
topics.unit: Unit 1 – Food and Digestion; G9 Unit 3
topics.concept: Nutrients, food tests, carbohydrates, digestion and cellular respiration.

subtopics.title: Nutrients, balanced diet and food tests
subtopics.concept: A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, vitamins, minerals and water (plus fibre). Fat leaves a translucent spot on paper. Carbohydrates contain C, H, O with H : O = 2 : 1; monosaccharides (CH₂O)ₙ, e.g. C₆H₁₂O₆. Polysaccharides (starch, glycogen, cellulose) are not sweet and insoluble. Too much saturated fat → atherosclerosis.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

subtopics.title: Digestive system
subtopics.concept: The cardiac sphincter guards the entrance to the stomach; the pyloric sphincter controls the passage of chyme from the stomach into the duodenum.

subtopics.title: Cellular respiration and fermentation
subtopics.concept: Aerobic respiration: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy (the main respiratory wastes). Anaerobic respiration in yeast = alcoholic fermentation (glucose → ethanol + CO₂) used for bread, beer, wine, 'mies' and 'suwa'; in muscle it gives lactic acid.

topics.title: Circulation, lymph and immunity
topics.concept: Heart and blood vessels, circulation routes, blood groups, lymphatic system and the immune system.

subtopics.title: Heart, circulation and blood vessels
subtopics.concept: Blood path: vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body. Systemic circulation is the largest circuit. Arteries: thick walls, no valves (except at their origin); veins: thin walls with valves; capillaries: walls one cell thick, no valves.

subtopics.title: ABO blood groups
subtopics.concept: Group O has anti-A and anti-B antibodies in the plasma; AB has none. Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant, i recessive: a child can be AB only if one parent supplies Iᴬ and the other Iᴮ.

textbook_refs.section: 1.4 Codominance and multiple alleles – ABO blood groups

subtopics.title: Lymphatic system and immunity
subtopics.concept: Lymph moves through lymphatic vessels mainly by muscular activity (contraction of skeletal muscles squeezing the vessels), with valves preventing backflow. Lymphatic tissue contains lymphocytes and macrophages (not erythrocytes). Antigens are macromolecules that trigger an immune response.

topics.title: Breathing and excretion
topics.concept: Breathing mechanism, external respiration, excretory organs and urinary system.

subtopics.title: Breathing and external respiration
subtopics.concept: External respiration = exchange of O₂ and CO₂ between the alveoli (lungs) and blood. Inhalation: diaphragm contracts and flattens, intercostal muscles raise ribs and sternum, thorax volume increases. Exhalation: diaphragm relaxes (domes up), ribs return, thorax volume decreases.

subtopics.title: Excretory organs and urinary system
subtopics.concept: Excretory organs: kidneys (urine), lungs (CO₂, water), skin (sweat), liver (urea, bile pigments). The heart is not an excretory organ. Urinary system: kidney → ureter → urinary bladder → urethra.

topics.title: Nervous and endocrine coordination
topics.concept: Neurons, brain, hormones and endocrine disorders.

subtopics.title: Neurons, synapse and brain
subtopics.concept: The myelin sheath of fatty cells makes the axon look like a necklace of sausage-shaped beads. Neurotransmitters cross the synaptic gap. The cerebrum makes up about 80 % of brain mass, has lobes, controls memory, and each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body. The spinal cord produces responses through reflex actions.

subtopics.title: Endocrine glands and hormones
subtopics.concept: Hormones are secretions of ductless endocrine glands, carried by blood (proteins, amines or steroids); enzymes are proteins secreted mainly by exocrine glands through ducts. Pituitary disorders: gigantism, dwarfism, acromegaly, diabetes insipidus (ADH); goitre is thyroid. Calcium is regulated by parathyroid hormone and calcitonin (thyroid). LH from the pituitary stimulates testosterone and progesterone. Drinking much water lowers ADH secretion.

topics.title: Skeleton, muscles, reproduction and homeostasis
topics.concept: Reproduction and development, skeletal and muscular systems, joints and homeostasis.

subtopics.title: Reproduction, cell division and development
subtopics.concept: Sexual reproduction involves fusion of gametes (two parents, variation); asexual reproduction involves one parent and no gametes (identical offspring). Somatic cells form by mitosis, gametes by meiosis (haploid: 48 → 24). The umbilical cord joins embryo and placenta: its vein brings food and oxygenated blood, its arteries take deoxygenated blood and wastes.

subtopics.title: Skeleton, joints and muscles
subtopics.concept: Endoskeleton: internal, grows smoothly without moulting, supports great size and weight. The human skeletal system = cartilages, ligaments and 206 bones; bones store minerals and fat, contain blood vessels, nerves and bone cells. Ligaments join bone to bone. Pivot joint (atlas–axis) turns the head. Skull = cranium + facial bones + ear ossicles; appendicular skeleton = limbs and girdles. Smooth muscle lines stomach, intestine, bladder and uterus; the heart is cardiac muscle. Muscles produce the force for movement.

subtopics.title: Homeostasis
subtopics.concept: Homeostasis keeps body temperature, blood glucose, water/salt balance, pH and CO₂ at set levels; endocrine, nervous, excretory and respiratory systems contribute, the reproductive system hardly at all.

topics.title: Plant systems and adaptations
topics.concept: Plant growth and hormones, seeds, stem structure and adaptations of plants and animals.

subtopics.title: Growth, seeds and plant hormones
subtopics.concept: Apical meristems at root and stem tips grow throughout life. The plumule becomes the shoot, the radicle the root. Dormant seeds are viable but inactive, controlled by internal and external factors, and help survival through stress. Gibberellins cause stem elongation (taller plants).

subtopics.title: Dicot stem structure
subtopics.concept: Dicot stem (outside → in): epidermis, cortex, vascular bundles in a ring (phloem outside, cambium between, xylem inside), pith in the centre.

subtopics.title: Adaptations of plants and animals
subtopics.concept: Hydrophytes live in water or waterlogged conditions. Succulents: leaves reduced to spines, green photosynthetic stem, water-storing stem, few sunken waxy stomata. Animals in cold: hormonal changes raising metabolic rate, insulation, hibernation, small ears.

topics.title: Genetics, evolution and ecology
topics.concept: Nucleic acids, protein synthesis, mutation, Mendelian genetics, evolution theories and ecology.

subtopics.title: DNA, RNA and mutation
subtopics.concept: DNA is a ladder: sugar–phosphate backbones are the sides, paired nitrogenous bases the steps. mRNA is transcribed from a DNA template. Gene mutations: substitution, deletion, insertion, inversion (a segment rotated through 180°).

subtopics.title: Genotypes
subtopics.concept: Homozygous: two identical alleles (TT, tt); heterozygous: two different alleles (Tt).

subtopics.title: Evolution theories and evidence
subtopics.concept: Darwin: overproduction, variation, struggle for existence, survival of the fittest (natural selection). Use and disuse is Lamarck's idea. Neo-Darwinism combines natural selection with genetics: mutation and recombination are the source of variation. Palaeontology studies fossils preserved in sedimentary rocks.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2 Theories of evolution – Lamarck and Darwin

subtopics.title: Levels of organisation, cycles, biomes and interactions
subtopics.concept: Ecosystem = lowest level including living and nonliving things. Carbon cycle: photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion (not evaporation). Biome vegetation is determined by temperature, rainfall and soil. Limiting factors: competition, predation, disease, migration (drought cannot limit ocean animals). Interactions between different species are inter-specific relations (predation, parasitism, competition, symbiosis).
